description: A sixteen-bit shift-register sequencer with a built-in quantiser and three Euclidean trigger generators, all of them running off one clock and one step count

params.text: Sets the chance that a step feeds a fresh random bit into the register instead of looping the bit round from the end; at the bottom the pattern repeats unchanged, at the top every step is new
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it repeats, 1 to 16, and that same count is the length of all three Euclidean patterns
Sets how many octaves the pitch output spans, 1 to 8, although the panel prints SCALE; which notes are allowed is chosen with the twelve buttons instead
Clears every bit in the register and sends the sequence back to its first step when pressed, which leaves the pitch output at its lowest note
Sets how many hits that Euclidean pattern spreads over the step count, 0 to 16; at 0 its output stays silent and at or above the step count every step fires
Puts that note into the set the pitch output is quantised to, or takes it out, with the lamp beside it lit while the note is in

inputs.text: Advances the sequence one step on each rising edge above 1V: the register shifts, the pitch is worked out again and the three Euclidean patterns are tested
Sends the sequence back to its first step on a rising edge above 1V, leaving the register's contents where they are

outputs.text: The quantised pitch, 1V per octave with 0V as C4; the register is read as a binary number and spread over the octave range
A 10V trigger 5ms long on every step where that Euclidean pattern has a hit

notes: nothing moves until a clock is patched to CLK, because the module has no clock of its own
the register starts empty, so the pitch output holds its lowest note until the Generate slider is raised and some steps have been clocked through
the module saves none of its own state: the register, the chosen notes and the three Euclidean shifts all return to their startup values on loading, the note set to C major
the two rows of lamps show the register's bits in red and each Euclidean pattern's hits in green, yellow and blue; they are lamps rather than controls and cannot be clicked for help
a shift other than zero rotates the lamps one way and the triggers the other, so the lit lamps then mark different steps from the ones that actually fire
menu: Euclid 1 Shift — rotates the first Euclidean pattern against the clock by 0 to 15 steps
Euclid 2 Shift — rotates the second Euclidean pattern against the clock by 0 to 15 steps
Euclid 3 Shift — rotates the third Euclidean pattern against the clock by 0 to 15 steps

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
